Title: Security update for the Java stack

Notes.Text: Security update for the Java stack
Notes.Title: Topic

Notes.Text:
This update for Java fixes the following issues:

This update introduces new libraries and refines existing Java tools to
improve security, compatibility, stability, and formatting.
    
ant (Updated to version 1.10.18):
    
- Security issues fixed:

  - CVE-2021-36374: Fixed excessive memory allocation when reading specially crafted ZIP archives or derived formats
    (bsc#1188469)
  - CVE-2025-7962: Fixed improper neutralization of line breaks to prevent SMTP injection (bsc#1246873)
  - CVE-2026-78254: Fixed path traversal in FTP and SCP tasks that could allow arbitrary file writes (bsc#1280015)

- Other changes and bugs fixed:

  * Breaking changes:
   
    + FTPS tasks now use encrypted data channels by default.
    + FTP and SCP tasks now prevent files or directories from being written outside the target directory by default.
 
  * Other changes:
    
    + Added package `ant-junit5` that allows tests to be launched and run using the JUnit 5 framework.
    + Improved support for reproducible builds by standardizing timestamps, file modification times, and timezone 
      handling.
    + Upgraded the jakarta.mail dependency to version 2.0.2.
    + Added an option to the 'record' task to create log files relative to the project directory.

  * Bugs fixed:
 
    + Fixed compatibility and startup issues when running on newer Java versions.
    + Fixed network handling issues in FTP and SCP tasks, including proper support for IPv6 addresses.
    + Improved security in email tasks by verifying TLS server certificates and enforcing STARTTLS encryption.
    + Improved report generation performance in JUnit launcher tasks.
    + Fixed regressions and edge cases in resource mapping, path conversion, and command execution.

json-simple (Updated to version 2.3.1):

- Updated to a newer version that makes reading and writing structured web data (JSON) safer and more reliable.
- Added a 'pretty-printing' feature to format web data so it is easier to read.
- Made reading and writing data safer when multiple tasks are running simultaneously.
- Made looking up data more flexible, allowing the tool to automatically handle different format types
  (like numbers and text).


junit5 (Updated to version 5.14.4):

- Fixed an issue where tests could conflict or run incorrectly when executed at the same time.
- Corrected test behavior on newer versions of Java so they run reliably.
- Improved test reports so that test names are clearer, unique, and easier to distinguish from one another.
- Added features to customize how test names are generated and better capture testing outputs.

maven-doxia, maven-doxia-sitetools (Updated to version 2.1.0):

- Added support for displaying the last modification date and author on
  generated web pages.
- Added support for displaying interactive diagrams (such as flowcharts or charts) directly on web pages.
- Improved formatting and layout for modern documents, including better tables, lists, and links.

maven-surefire, maven-surefire-plugins (Updated to version 3.5.6):

- Fixed a bug that caused software testing tasks to fail abruptly with an unexpected error [bsc#1273185].
- Added timestamps to testing reports so you can see exactly when tests ran.
- Made running multiple tests at the same time much more reliable, preventing mixed-up report results.
- Added the ability to immediately stop testing once a failure is detected (saving time).

objectweb-asm (Updated to version 9.10.1):

- Added support for newer Java versions, including bytecode support up to Java 27.
- Prevented out-of-memory errors when processing invalid or corrupted class files.
- Improved bytecode analysis and verification to correctly handle valid Java code and prevent unexpected analysis errors
- Improved compliance with FIPS 140-3 security standards during class serialization.
- Corrected package import ranges to prevent dependency conflicts in OSGi environments.
- Fixed unexpected crashes and errors in code generation and inspection utilities.

plexus-archiver (Updated to version 4.14.0):

- Added support for following symbolic links when collecting files for archives.
- Reduced memory usage when creating ZIP archives to prevent out-of-memory errors during large builds.
- Fixed an issue where reading file attributes on Windows systems could cause unexpected errors.
- Improved ZIP archive handling, fixing checksum calculation errors, negative timestamp issues, and file permissions.
- Replaced compression components with Apache Commons Compress to eliminate vulnerable dependencies.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated dependencies, including commons-io to 2.22.0, xz to 1.12, and zstd-jni to 1.5.7-15.

plexus-build-api (Updated to version 1.2.0):

- Updated dependencies for compatibility with modern build and injection tools.

plexus-cipher (Updated to version 2.1.0):

- Updated dependencies for compatibility with modern build and injection tools.

plexus-classworlds (Updated to version 2.12.1):

- Fixed file pattern matching (glob matching) when loading classes and resources.
- Restored backward compatibility with legacy Maven 2 configurations.
- Added support for registering filtered class realms.
- Implemented clean resource shutdown support (Closeable) for class loaders.
- Added support for the PPC64LE architecture.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated dependencies, including jakarta.xml.bind-api, log4j-api, and ant.

plexus-compiler (Updated to version 2.17.1):

- Fixed a security issue (Zip Slip) that could allow arbitrary file overwrite during archive extraction.
- Fixed an unexpected crash (ConcurrentModificationException) when processing compiler arguments concurrently.
- Fixed compiler diagnostics and warning reporting to ensure multi-line messages and warning categories are properly
  displayed.
- Fixed Java version detection when custom options or newer Java versions are present.
- Fixed an issue where the Eclipse Java Compiler (ECJ) failed to detect annotation processors configured in the
  processor path.
- Added support for quoting compiler argument files to safely handle paths containing spaces.
- Fixed cross-drive file path handling on Windows systems.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated dependencies, including Google Guava to 33.7.1 and Eclipse Java Compiler (ECJ) to 3.46.100.

plexus-containers (Updated to version 2.2.0):

- Added the plexus-metadata-generator Ant task and command-line interface to generate component metadata.
- Added the plexus-metadata-generator-ant package capability.

plexus-i18n (Updated to version 1.2.0):

- Corrected language translation lookup to prevent unintentionally falling back to the system default locale.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated internal dependencies.

plexus-interactivity (Updated to version 1.6.0):

- Upgraded the terminal reader dependency to JLine 3 for improved console and terminal interaction.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated dependencies, including Sisu Inject to 1.1.0 and Guice to 5.1.0.

plexus-interpolation (Updated to version 1.30.0):

- Fixed caching issues in string and regular expression interpolators to significantly improve evaluation performance
  and consistency.
- Added support for feedback value sources and delimiter tracking.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated internal dependencies.

plexus-io (Updated to version 3.8.0):

- Improved performance by caching Unix user and group lookups.
- Fixed file handling to properly follow symbolic links when configured.
- Fixed an issue where temporary files were left unclosed, preventing file-not-found errors.
- Improved resilience when querying file attributes on network file systems.
- Added support for tracking hard-link identities for unchanged files.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated dependencies, including commons-io to 2.22.0, plexus-utils to 3.6.2, and Sisu Inject to 1.1.0.

plexus-languages (Updated to version 1.6.0):

- Replaced the source code parser with JavaParser for improved language support and modern Java compatibility.
- Added support for newer Java versions, including JDK 23 and JDK 24 bytecode.
- Improved the speed of detecting Java class file versions.
- Added validation to detect and report duplicate modules on the module path.
- Updated dependencies, including ObjectWeb ASM to 9.10.1.

plexus-sec-dispatcher (Updated to version 2.0):

- Modernized component injection by using standard javax.inject annotations.
- Updated dependencies for compatibility with modern Sisu tools.

plexus-utils (Updated to version 4.1.0):

- Breaking change: File scanning no longer excludes '.gitignore' and '.cvsignore' files by default.
- Fixed a security issue (Zip Slip) that could allow arbitrary file overwrite during archive extraction.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated internal dependencies.

plexus-velocity (Updated to version 2.4.0):

- Reduced runtime dependency requirements by eliminating unnecessary injection components.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated dependencies to secure releases, including Apache Velocity Engine to 2.4.1 and Commons Lang to 3.20.0.

plexus-xml (Updated to version 3.1.0):

- Fixed XML parsing issues when reading documents in UTF-8 (without BOM) and ISO-8859-1 encodings.
- Added Java Module System (JPMS) support for compatibility with modern Java versions.
- Updated internal dependencies, including plexus-utils to 4.0.2.


New package dependencies distributed:

- apache-commons-digester3: XML-to-Java object mapping library; required at
  runtime by `velocity-tools`.
- javaparser: Java source code parser and abstract syntax tree library;
  required at runtime by `plexus-languages`.
- antlr: Parser generator for reading, processing, and translating
  structured text; required at runtime by `ant` (`ant-antlr`).
- jakarta-mail: Implementation of the Jakarta Mail API for email handling
  (addresses CVE-2025-7962); required at runtime by `ant` (`ant-jakartamail`).
- jakarta-activation: Framework for handling MIME data types and extensible
  data content; required at runtime by `jakarta-mail` and `ant`
  (`ant-jakartamail`).
- univocity-parsers: Fast CSV, TSV, and fixed-width tabular text parser
  collection; required at runtime by `ant` (`ant-junit5`) and `junit5`.
- opentest4j: Common exception and test assertion abstraction for JVM
  testing frameworks; required at runtime by `ant` (`ant-junit5`) and `junit5`.
- picocli: Annotation-based command-line interface parser; required at
  runtime by `junit5`.
- assertj-core: Fluent assertion library for Java testing; required at
  runtime by `junit5`.
- plexus-build-api0: Compatibility API layer for Plexus build tooling;
  required at runtime by `plexus-build-api`.
- qdox: High-speed parser for extracting class, interface, and Javadoc
  metadata; required at runtime by `plexus-containers`
  (`plexus-component-metadata`).
- bsf: Bean Scripting Framework for running scripting languages from Java;
  required at runtime by `ant` (`ant-apache-bsf`).
- jdepend: Metric generator analyzing Java package design and dependencies;
  required at runtime by `ant` (`ant-jdepend`).
- javassist: Java bytecode manipulation and analysis toolkit; required at
  runtime by `javaparser`.
- ant-contrib: Additional tasks, condition handlers, and control-flow logic
  for Apache Ant; optional runtime companion for `ant`.
- byte-buddy: Runtime code generation and bytecode manipulation library;
  required at runtime by `junit5` and `ant-junit5`.
- velocity-tools: Reusable tools and view support helpers for the Apache
  Velocity template engine; standalone runtime library for template-driven web
  applications.
- zstd-jni: JNI bindings providing fast and high-ratio lossless compression
  via Zstandard; required at runtime by `plexus-archiver`.

Vulnerabilities.Description: When reading a specially crafted ZIP archive, or a derived formats, an Apache Ant build can be made to allocate large amounts of memory that leads to an out of memory error, even for small inputs. This can be used to disrupt builds using Apache Ant. Commonly used derived formats from ZIP archives are for instance JAR files and many office files. Apache Ant prior to 1.9.16 and 1.10.11 were affected.

Vulnerabilities.Description:
The ftp and scp tasks of Apache Ant can download files from a remote server. A malicious server can provide relative paths that allow it to write outside of the dedicated target directory for the download, making it possible to overwrite files of the attacker's choice using the permissions of the user running Ant in versions prior to Ant 1.10.18. 




In order to exploit this vulnerability, the server would either have to be malicious  or be subject to a machine-in-the-middle attack. Additionally  in the case of scp or the ftp task using ftps the server must pass the server identity checks performed by the tasks.




For ftp tasks not using ftps a malicious server could act as a machine-in-the-middle to provide malicious files.




Starting with Ant 1.10.18 both tasks will prevent writing outside of the destination directory by default. An option is available to disable this behavior in the unlikely case that the  old behavior is required by existing build files.




Mitigations:




Users of scp and ftp (when using ftps) in any version of Ant should not bypass server identity checks. Users of ftp not using ftps should switch to ftps where possible.




All users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Ant 1.10.18, which fixes this issue.
